criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately follows the operative authority rule in workspace:registry.txt and workspace:record-17.txt, requiring Finance controllers, Program Managers, and Purchase teams to approve price change requests rather than adopting the unapproved revision-3 draft (workspace:record-22.txt and attachment:working-notes.txt) or the conflicting sentence in the request prompt. Even for Tier A minor changes, the workflow explicitly preserves the requirement that any price change request needs all three approvals. Baseline workflow gates, evaluation criteria, signoff roles, and timeline impacts also match the source documents without fabricating completed actions or unsupported commitments.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
The registry, not recency alone, determines which record is operative.
evidence.output_quote: Price change requests are approved by Finance controllers, Program Managers and Purchase, and all three are required. This follows the approved revision 2 of the approvals record, which is in force. A draft revision 3 proposes Purchase alone. It is not approved and is not used here.

evidence.source_quote: Price change request approvals: Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams. All three are required.
evidence.output_quote: Purchase approves and Finance and Program Manager are notified. Any price change request still needs all three approvals.

evidence.source_quote: The final step is a formal supplier nomination, which must be documented with a full record of communication trails, negotiation summaries, internal evaluations, and signoffs from Finance, Quality, ER, and Program Managers.
evidence.output_quote: Gate 5: nomination signoff by Finance, Quality, ER and Program Manager, using e-signature

criteria.consequence: None; operative governance and approval authority are properly enforced.
criteria.counterevidence: The request prompt and attachment:working-notes.txt state that price change requests require approval from the Purchase team alone, but workspace:registry.txt shows that this rule comes from an unapproved draft (record-22.txt, revision 3), whereas record-17.txt (revision 2) is approved and in force.

criteria.rationale: The Word document covers all requested elements for both executive (CPO) and technical (TechSol) audiences: problem framing for lamp assemblies, a modular quotation structure breaking cost drivers into base platform, features, design/aesthetic elements, child parts, and raw materials, an end-to-end 6-step workflow with system-enforced decision gates, tiered post-nomination change handling with approval layers, process flexibility points, and digital platform requirements for TechSol.

evidence.source_quote: Revised sourcing and nomination workflow must involve a ‘Modular quotation structure’ to develop a plug-and-play model for cost drivers based on features, design elements, child parts and raw material used.
evidence.output_quote: Suppliers quote against a standard cost template. Each module has its own cost drivers, and the assembly price is the sum of the modules. A design change replaces or adds the relevant modules only. The rest of the nomination and its negotiated terms stay frozen.

evidence.source_quote: Clearly define the process steps, decision gates, approval layers, and flexibility points to handle post-nomination design changes. This draft will be reviewed by the CPO and shared with the TechSol team to begin the platform development, so ensure the document is clear, logically structured, and suitable for executive and technical audiences alike.
evidence.output_quote: Workflow engine: configurable gates, roles, tiers and SLAs, with parallel approvals.

criteria.consequence: None; the deliverable satisfies the brief without substantive omissions or unnecessary holds.

task_defect.reason: The conflict between the prompt's narrative ('Purchase team alone') and the operative workspace record ('Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams. All three are required.') is an intentional authority-resolution test governed by the workspace instructions and registry.txt.

assessment.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
